newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador group says it will free foreign hostages.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador group says it will free foreign hostages.

text.p: An indigenous group in Ecuador said on Friday it would free two foreign scientists it has been holding hostage, after the oil company Compania General de Combustibles (CGC) agreed to stop production plans in the group's territory.

Indigenous leader Miguel Vargas told a local radio station that his Ashuar tribe and the Argentine company would sign a document on Friday night allowing the release of the hostages, one American and one British, on Saturday.

He said the company would suspend its oil exploitation plans in the Sahime territory, controlled by the Ashuar, and pay them $1,300 (five million sucres) to cover the cost of caring for the scientists who were kidnapped last Saturday.

"We've held a meeting, a peaceful dialogue, and as a result we've come up with a document in which both sides agree that (CGC) will halt oil activities, ask for authorization to enter the territory and pay five million sucres," Vargas said.

British citizen Victor Morley Read and American Mark Thurber were taken hostage after they entered the Sahime area, some 150 miles (240 km) south of Quito, to carry out environmental impact studies in the Amazon jungle ahead of CGC oil production. They were contracted out to CGC by U.S. firm Walsh.

CGG did not immediately comment on the deal announced by the Ashuar, who on Thursday had demanded a ransom of $2 million to free the hostages and as compensation for what they considered to be the theft of ecological information.
